headline: Microsoft warns that AI is collapsing the gap between a patch's release and its exploitation, pushing enterprises to deploy updates faster than monthly cycles ever assumed.

emerging_trends.text: Microsoft is telling administrators to shrink their patch windows because AI now finds and weaponizes flaws faster than monthly update cadences assume, and the company expects its own AI bug-hunting to swell the update count.
Voice-phishing crews like Helix keep proving that a well-placed phone call beats multifactor authentication, walking data straight out of SharePoint and Microsoft 365 tenants.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Vishing Crews Loot SharePoint and Microsoft 365

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep burrowing into the software supply chain through dormant GitHub accounts and poisoned packages, pushing GitHub to disable npm install scripts by default.
emerging_trends.topic_title: GitHub and npm Supply-Chain Abuse Widens

topics.title: AI Compresses the Patch-to-Exploit Window
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft rewrote its Windows update guidance on July 10 to urge shorter deployment timelines, warning that AI shrinks the time attackers need to exploit a freshly patched flaw, and said it expects more monthly updates as it leans on AI to hunt bugs in its own code.
topics.summary: Microsoft advises organizations to accelerate rollout of monthly security updates, particularly on devices that tolerate short deployment windows, as AI compresses the interval between disclosure and mass exploitation; June 2026 already delivered over 200 CVEs, including 116 for Windows 11.

sources.title: Microsoft is rewriting Windows patch guidance because of AI
Microsoft expects more Windows security updates from AI-discovered flaws
July 2026 Patch Tuesday forecast: Is CVE tracking still practical?

topics.title: Vishing Crews Loot SharePoint and Microsoft 365
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer identified Helix on July 9, a new data-extortion group that pairs voice phishing, device-code phishing, and MFA abuse to steal data from SharePoint environments, joining Okta's O-UNC-066 crew that phones Microsoft 365 users to enroll rogue Entra passkeys.
topics.summary: Both Helix and O-UNC-066 lean on identity-focused social engineering—a phone call that steers victims to fake Microsoft Entra ID login pages or coaxes them through passkey enrollment—to seize accounts for data theft and extortion; enforce phishing-resistant MFA and verify IT callers.

sources.title: New Helix vishing group emerges in SharePoint data theft attacks
Okta Warns of Vishing Attacks Targeting Microsoft 365 Customers
Hackers Use Fake Microsoft Entra Passkey Enrollment to Gain Microsoft 365 Access

topics.title: BlackCat's Insider Negotiators Head to Prison
topics.latest_developments: A US court sentenced Angelo Martino, 41, a former DigitalMint ransomware negotiator, to 70 months for conspiring with the BlackCat/ALPHV gang to extort victims in 2023, making him the third US security professional imprisoned in the scheme.
topics.summary: Martino, hired to negotiate on behalf of ransomware victims, instead worked with BlackCat operators and two other cybersecurity professionals to launch attacks; his sentencing caps a run of insider betrayals inside the incident-response industry.

sources.title: Third US Security Expert Sentenced to Prison for Helping Ransomware Gang
Former ransomware negotiator gets 4 years for BlackCat attacks
Ransomware Negotiator Gets 70 Months in Prison for Aiding BlackCat Attacks

topics.title: GitHub and npm Supply-Chain Abuse Widens
topics.latest_developments: GitHub shipped npm 12 on July 9 with install scripts disabled by default and granular access tokens deprecated, the same day Datadog flagged dormant 'ghost' GitHub accounts enumerating corporate organizations through the API and SecurityWeek exposed a network of 200 GitHub repositories loading PowerShell malware.
topics.summary: Attackers exploit developer trust in GitHub and npm—scraping corporate repos through years-old accounts, hosting Go-and-PowerShell malware loaders across 200 repositories, and slipping stealers into packages—prompting npm 12 to make automatic install scripts opt-in; audit tokens and pin dependencies.

sources.title: npm 12 Disables Install Scripts by Default to Reduce Supply Chain Risk
Dormant GitHub Accounts Help Attackers Blend In While Mapping Corporate Orgs
Network of 200 GitHub Repositories Used for Malware Infection

topics.title: GigaWiper Bundles Wiper, Fake Ransomware, and Spyware
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft dissected GigaWiper on July 9, a Windows backdoor that bolts three older destructive tools into one operator-selectable menu.
topics.summary: GigaWiper offers its operator a standalone disk wiper, a multi-pass overwrite of the Windows drive, and fake ransomware that scrambles files with a key it never saves, making recovery impossible; it targets machines for system-level sabotage rather than payment.

sources.title: New GigaWiper Windows Backdoor Bundles Disk Wiping, Fake Ransomware, and Spyware
GigaWiper Combines Multiple Malware for System-Level Sabotage

topics.title: Laser and BitLocker Bugs Threaten Crypto Hardware
topics.latest_developments: Ledger's Donjon team showed on July 10 that a precisely timed laser pulse aimed at a Tangem wallet card's chip resets the card's password to anything the attacker picks, handing over the coins, while Dark Reading detailed fresh bugs in a Microsoft BitLocker security wrapper that put crypto ATMs at risk.
topics.summary: The Tangem attack demands physical access and specialized equipment, so it endangers stolen or lost cards rather than every owner, and the unpatchable chip design leaves no fix; the BitLocker wrapper flaws expose organizations and ATMs to compromise.

sources.title: Laser Attack Resets Tangem Wallet Passwords on Cards That Can't Be Patched
Fresh ATM Crypto Software Bugs: Jackpot or Bust?

business_politics.latest_developments: Trump declared the U.S.-Iran ceasefire 'over' yet said Washington and Tehran agreed to keep negotiating, and markets calmed as Treasury yields rose and oil steadied on fading escalation fears.
